draft.title: Connotation
card: the basic dictionary meaning of a word. Slim and skinny both denote a person with little body fat.
the feeling or idea a word carries beyond its basic meaning. Slim feels positive and suggests healthy or graceful. Skinny can feel negative and suggest thin in an unhealthy way.
Words with a similar denotation can have different connotations. Compare house and home, or cheap and affordable.
Writers choose words for their connotations on purpose. The choice shapes how a reader feels about a person, place or thing.
draft.remember: Similar words can mean the same thing but feel different, and writers pick the feeling they want.

a.q: Which sentence best explains what connotation is?
opts: The feeling a word carries beyond its basic meaning
The basic dictionary meaning of a word
The way a word is spelled or pronounced
The job a word does in a sentence
a.why: Connotation is the feeling or idea attached to a word. The basic dictionary meaning is its denotation, which is the most tempting wrong option because the two ideas sit side by side.
a.clue: Think about feelings, not dictionary meanings.

b.q: A reporter describes a local footballer as stubborn. A different reporter calls the same player determined. What is the main difference between the two words?
opts: Stubborn has a negative feeling, determined a positive one
Stubborn means the player is older than determined does
Determined has a different dictionary meaning from stubborn
Determined is a more formal word, so it is always correct
b.why: Both words describe someone who does not give up, but stubborn feels negative and determined feels positive. The meaning is close, so the difference lies in the connotation, not in the dictionary definition.
b.clue: Both words describe the same player. What differs is how each one makes you feel.

a.best: The feeling a word carries beyond its basic meaning

b.best: Stubborn has a negative feeling, determined a positive one

The clue 'What differs is how each one makes you feel' matches only the right option (the only one about feeling), so it gives the answer away.

a.q: Which pair of words has a similar basic meaning but different connotations?
opts: Curious and nosy
Happy and sad
Run and walk
Tall and heavy
a.why: Curious and nosy both describe someone who wants to know things, so their denotation is similar. Curious feels positive and nosy feels negative. Run and walk can tempt, but they name different actions, so their basic meanings differ.
a.clue: First check whether each pair could describe the very same thing.

b.q: A reporter describes a local footballer as stubborn. A different reporter calls the same player determined. What is the main difference between the two words?
opts: Stubborn sounds negative, and determined sounds positive
Stubborn sounds positive, and determined sounds negative
They have quite different dictionary meanings
Determined is more formal, so it is the correct word
b.why: Both words describe someone who does not give up, so the basic meaning is close. Stubborn suggests being difficult, which feels negative, while determined suggests strength, which feels positive. The reversed option is tempting, but it swaps the two feelings.
b.clue: Which word would the player rather read about themselves?

b.best: Stubborn sounds negative, and determined sounds positive
